title: LLM-Varianced NPC Interactions - Performance Feedback Needed
author: WhopperitoJr
selftext:
Hi all,

I am working on building a historical sim game using an Unreal Engine plugin I developed, with the goal of releasing a game with NPCs and events built from the ground up using local LLMs for generation. I have been working on a demo for a couple months to show one initial way I would like to include LLMs.

While the demo works quite well for me in the editor, once I package the game, the LLM response times lengthen quite a bit, and sometimes times out completely. I am working off of a 3060Ti with 8 GB of VRAM, so I am looking for some users with higher-end GPUs to give this a try and see if the difference in response times is due to my equipment, or an inherent wrinkle to iron out.

If you have a Windows machine and would be willing to give it a test, I have a .zip available for download [on itch.io](https://swamprabbit-labs.itch.io/salutatio-demo-v1) which contains both the game files, and the infrastructure needed to run the LLM alongside it (though the plugin system launches this in the background, you do not have to do anything to get it running yourself).

If you try it out, it would be great to hear your notes on what the wait time was for the game to load, and any hangups you may have run into.

Also, it would be great to hear from other developers if you have run into similar post-packaging issues; are there any solutions or mitigations I should consider?

comments.author: AxiosXiphos
comments.body:
Seems interesting. But i'm not too keen on installing random files or LLM connections from an unknown source....

  
Apologies I don't know how you get round that.

replies.author: WhopperitoJr
replies.body:
Totally understand! If it changes your mind, it’s essentially a typical Unreal package that includes llama.cpp for the local server and Gemma 3-4B as the model. It cannot touch anything outside Unreal, and will work with the internet completely disconnected. The only connection is within your own machine. If you look on my itchio site, I have some other LLM projects with 50+ downloads that function the same way, and I haven’t seen any issues related to security or air gaps. The product description on itchio links to more documentation if you’d like to see how the code itself works (I don’t want to break any rules so I did not link it in my OP).

Also should be fine to download, scan, and run in a  sandboxed environment or virtual machine (although response times may increase).

replies.author: Holiday-Elevator-180
replies.body: What about the performance of the Gemma 3-4B model in local machine?, although it seems that Gemma 3-4B is light a LLM model, the requirements of your game are demanding 8Gb, memory 16GB +, etc.

replies.author: WhopperitoJr
replies.body:
I am running the exported package using the Gemma 3 model. For anything outside UE, or within the editor, it works great, I am getting 18-19 tokens and second. It is a light model in and of itself, but running the model alongside UE5 still takes up a lot of VRAM, and generation rate for me drops.

I am hoping to identify if this is just a hardware issue, or if there are some further optimizations I can make to make the packaged game play more like it did in-editor.

comments.author: SeekingSpire
comments.body: I'd offer to test this myself if I wasn't so busy.. seems like the sort of idea that might benefit from Karpathy's autoleaning project if you really want to stick with local models. Maybe openrouter API calls to the cheapest possible models ad supported (or use can input their own openrouter key) - might be easier for everyone involved.

replies.author: WhopperitoJr
replies.body: Yeah I am thinking of doing more experimenting with a cloud setup, if nothing else so I can understand better how it performs in my system. Ideally, I can still solve this loading problem so that local models are responsive, too

comments.author: Radiant_Mind33
comments.body:
It's interesting, mainly because I've already thought better of the whole plan. 

The Unreal overhead is real, and I'm told you can hard fence the VRAM usage but idk because I always come back to asking, why Unreal for this at all? You can't expect people to have 8 gigs of ram just to talk to an NPC. And that's not even considering the logic leaks and immersion breaking.

If I ever did it, the AI would never talk directly to the player. IOW, the AI should just do logic in the background like a dungeon master. Not an NPC.

replies.author: WhopperitoJr
replies.body:
It’s less that I am developing an unreal game and decided to build this in UE, and more that I already have the plugin available on UE, and now I am scaffolding out a full game to help iron out the difficult use cases. The full scale game would have several different game modes that utilize LLMs in different ways. This demo is just one small slice of a much larger cake.

I’ve also designed this for background use like you described, and have a few designs for setting up background LLMs for diplomacy, event generation, etc. I have a system where you can set up tags and actions that the brain can read and write, so it turns into basically an agent. It’d be great to hear of other uses you’d use this, or something like this, for!

comments.author: WhoisAizenn
comments.body:
might be worth considering offloading inference entirely rather than fighting local packaging issues. ZeroGPU has a waitlist open for distributed inference, which could help with the latency spikes. RunPod serverless is another option that works now but gets pricey fast.

honestly though for a game shipping to end users, you might want to look at smaller quantized models that run consistant on consumer hardware.

replies.author: WhopperitoJr
replies.body: I already have non-local setups like this, but my work is mainly focused on getting local to be more functional. My preference is to avoid dependency on third party services, especially paid ones. I have a few other local-only demos that did not have this issue so I am just hoping to get more technical information from others familiar with Unreal instead of trying a wholly different approach.

comments.author: trikboomie
comments.body:

replies.author: WhopperitoJr
replies.body: Definitely looks interesting but that plugin seems to be for Unity and I am not able to completely port over my Unreal project into Unity, that would be an awful headache. Plus this seems much more limited than my current framework, so I feel like I’d be taking a step back, especially since I already solved the problem my post mentioned.

replies.author: trikboomie
replies.body: Curious to see what your npc design system looks like

replies.author: WhopperitoJr
replies.body:
I have a similar connection bridge but I also have built data assets and traffic control systems that can be easily used within Unreal. A recursive memory system that reads and writes to the same NPC profile. And some built-in utility ai connections. You can read more about the system here:

https://swamprabbitlabs.com/support/
